title: Shared flight-plan intent
summary: Bounded portable plans with explicit per-node review.

blocks.text: flight.plans@1.0.0 captures and validates inert SI plan archives for up to 64 ships and 16 nodes per ship. Every node identifies its body and time. No thrust, warp, arming or execution state is stored. Evaluate through the selected public motion/orbit/surface/rails contracts; evaluateAsync progressively validates exact-time coasts through moving SOIs and contact checks; evaluate retains fast same-body compatibility. Cross-body hosts declare predictionFeatures.endTime. Samples and encounter snapshots use the initial translating nonrotating frame, including velocity conversion. Cancel generators to release forecasts and cloned contexts. Headless use needs no UI, camera, prediction, audio or split-screen module.

Optional node.targetOrbit stores ordered finite nonnegative periapsisAltitude/apoapsisAltitude in metres above the node body reference radius. It is portable inert intent, with no execution/arming permission. An explicitly authorized arrival reviewer may use it to propose a capture from actual flight; ordinary evaluate/evaluateAsync never retime nodes or execute controls. Older nodes without this goal remain readable.

Explicit plans allow at most100 Julian years after their epoch, while default display prediction retains its shorter cap. Optional boolean node.finite requests selected finite-controller evaluation through evaluateAsync; synchronous evaluate returns a progressive-evaluation diagnostic for these nodes. The host binds its selected flight.maneuver-burn controller through withBurns; presentation providers do not import platform services. Absence never silently treats finite intent as an impulse. simulateBurn and refineCapture are detached cancellable generators using the supplied selected controller, terrain/SOI safety, bounded work and max(.01m,radius*1e-7) capture-apsis tolerance. No live authority or execution permission is modified. Absolute-time comparisons account for double-precision spacing at multi-year epochs.
